mainTopic: Comparing שבת and יום טוב limits on moving produce, and whether one may cover items that are not usable on שבת
overview: The גמרא compares the strictness of שבת and יום טוב using two rules. One rule is about clearing sacks on שבת to make room for guests or learning. The other is about lowering produce from a roof on יום טוב. It asks whether each limit carries over to the other day, such as emptying everything, moving from roof to roof, or using ropes and ladders. For each question it argues both ways, and the rope-and-ladder question ends in תיקו. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's permission to cover produce. עולא allows covering even bricks. רבי יצחק allows covering only usable items, because a כלי may be moved only for something that may itself be moved. Proofs from the משנה's wording are pushed aside. Then challenges against רבי יצחק come from a leak, bricks, stones and a beehive, and each is answered by showing the item is really usable. The beehive answer leads to a long back-and-forth about honey in winter, planning ahead, and whether the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון. The גמרא settles that it follows רבי יהודה, about a hive with side openings, and starts correcting the ברייתא's wording, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The storeroom rule on שבת, explained by שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about שבת: you may not do 'the storeroom.' שמואל explains that this means you may not empty the storeroom completely, because you might then level the holes in the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Elsewhere we learned: 'But not the storeroom.' שמואל explained: you may not finish emptying the whole storeroom, because you might come to level holes in the floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known rule about שבת to set up a question. The question about יום טוב comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה allows moving sacks of produce on שבת to make room for guests or for the study hall. שמואל says the limit is emptying the storeroom completely. Once the floor is bare, a person might fill in its holes, and that is a real מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: To level out holes in the floor

phrases.english: There we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת שבת about clearing sacks of produce to make room for guests or for learning.

phrases.english: "But not the storeroom."
And Shmuel said:
What does "but not the storeroom" mean?

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא יִגְמוֹר אֶת הָאוֹצָר כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: But he may not finish clearing the entire storeroom,
lest he come to level out holes in the floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that compares this rule to our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת you may not empty a storeroom completely, in case you come to level the holes in its floor.

steps.title: Does the storeroom limit also apply on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the rule against emptying everything also applies to lowering produce on יום טוב. It gives two possible ways to argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule here? Maybe on שבת it is forbidden because שבת is strict, but יום טוב is lighter, so it is fine. Or maybe: there, where the clearing was for the study hall, you still said no; here, where there is no study hall involved, is it not all the more so forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the 'don't empty it all' limit carries over to our יום טוב case. It lays out one argument to allow it and one argument to forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the limit exists only because שבת is stricter, so on the lighter יום טוב it falls away. Side two is a כל שכן: the שבת case had a מצוה reason (making room for learning), and it was still forbidden. Our case has no מצוה reason at all, so it should be forbidden even more. The גמרא leaves the question open here.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding up learning in the study hall

steps.confusionAlert: The second side is not saying יום טוב is stricter than שבת. It says that a case with no מצוה reason deserves less leniency.

phrases.english: Here, what is the rule?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our case of lowering produce from the roof on יום טוב. Can he empty the whole roof?

phrases.english: Is it there, on Shabbat, that it is forbidden,
because it is strict,
but on Yom Tov, which is lighter,
it is fine.
Or perhaps:
there, where learning in the study hall is being held up,
you said no;
here, where no learning in the study hall is being held up,
is it not all the more so forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's שבת rule to our יום טוב case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on emptying the whole storeroom also apply to lowering produce on יום טוב?

steps.title: Lowering produce on יום טוב is allowed only on the same roof
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב. רב נחמן limits this to a skylight on the same roof, not moving the produce from one roof to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we learned: one may lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב. רב נחמן said: this was taught only for the same roof, but not from one roof to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a limit from our own יום טוב משנה. This sets up the reverse question: does that limit also apply on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן narrows the משנה's permission. You may lower produce through a skylight in the roof where it already lies. You may not carry it over to a different roof to use that roof's skylight.

phrases.english: And here we learned:

phrases.aramaic: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּירוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may lower produce through a skylight on Yom Tov,
and Rav Nachman said:
They taught this only about that same roof,
but from one roof to another roof, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second comparison, this time going from יום טוב to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב you may lower produce only through a skylight in the same roof, not by carrying it from roof to roof.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that you may not carry from roof to roof, even when the roofs are at the same height.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: one may not carry from one roof to another, even when the roofs are level with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב נחמן's limit with a ברייתא that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes even further. Even level roofs, where there is no climbing up or down, still may not be used for moving the produce across. This confirms רב נחמן's 'same roof only' rule.

phrases.english: And it was also taught this way in a baraita:
One may not carry from one roof to another roof
even when their roofs are level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's limit.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that produce may not be moved from roof to roof
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: אין מטלטלין מגג לגג אפילו כשגגותיהן שוין

steps.title: Does the roof-to-roof limit also apply on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, in the שבת case of moving sacks, you may carry them from one place to another. Maybe people don't take יום טוב seriously enough, so it needs extra limits that שבת does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, what is the rule? (All the more so on שבת, which is strict? Or perhaps:) Here it is forbidden because יום טוב is lighter, and people would come to treat it lightly. But שבת is strict and people would not treat it lightly, so it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the reverse question: does the יום טוב limit of 'not from roof to roof' carry over to the שבת sacks case? It closes by spelling out the argument for allowing it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think שבת, being stricter, should be at least as limited. But the reason here is different. יום טוב needs a fence because people see it as light and might start disregarding it. שבת is already respected, so no such fence is needed, and moving the sacks would be permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Here being 'lighter' makes יום טוב MORE restricted, not less. A day people take lightly needs extra fences so it won't be disregarded.
steps.whatToRemember: Both questions turn on one idea: being 'strict' or 'light' can cut either way. It depends on the reason behind each rule (fear of doing a מלאכה, a מצוה need, or people treating the day lightly).

phrases.english: There, what is the rule?
phrases.notes: 'There' is the שבת case of moving sacks for guests or learning. May he move them from place to place?

phrases.english: (All the more so on Shabbat, which is strict,
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets appear in the standard printed גמרא, but the corrected text leaves them out.

phrases.english: or perhaps:)
it is here that it is forbidden
because Yom Tov is lighter,
and people would come to treat it lightly;
but Shabbat, which is strict,
and people would not come to treat it lightly,
it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the roof-to-roof limit back onto the שבת case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May the sacks be moved from one place to another on שבת, given that on יום טוב produce may not be moved from roof to roof?

steps.title: The other side: maybe שבת is even stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the second side of the question about carrying sacks from place to place on שבת: if it is forbidden on יום טוב even though produce may be lost, it should be even more forbidden on שבת, where nothing is lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe we should say the opposite: here, on יום טוב, the produce could be ruined, and still you say he may not move it from roof to roof. There, on שבת, nothing will be ruined, so isn't it all the more forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing the question from Step 5. It now argues the other way: maybe moving the sacks on שבת is even more forbidden than on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the reason to allow it on שבת was that people take יום טוב lightly, so יום טוב needs extra limits. Here the counter-reasoning is a קל וחומר. On יום טוב the produce is at risk and moving it from roof to roof is still forbidden, so on שבת, with no loss at all, it should surely be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
Loss of produce, meaning the fruit being ruined by rain.
Is it not all the more so? This is the language of a קל וחומר.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: מָה הָכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶפְסֵד פֵּירוֹת
phrases.english: Or perhaps: if here, where there is a loss of produce,
you say no,
there, where there is no loss of produce,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא: מָה הָכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶפְסֵד פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question opened in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether carrying sacks from one place to another on שבת is permitted or even more forbidden than on יום טוב.

steps.title: New question: ropes and ladders for the sacks on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב we learned that produce may not be lowered with a rope through windows or carried down ladders. The גמרא asks whether the same applies to moving sacks on שבת, since there the need is to keep the בית המדרש from being disrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we learned: he may not lower the produce with a rope through the windows, and he may not bring it down by way of ladders. There, on שבת, what is the law? Maybe it is forbidden here on יום טוב because no learning in the בית המדרש is being disrupted. But on שבת, where learning in the בית המדרש would be disrupted, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second, similar question, this time about lowering things with ropes or ladders. Here it gives the side that leans toward allowing it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, using windows and ladders is too much work just to save produce. On שבת the sacks are cleared for a מצוה, to make room for learning. So maybe the מצוה reason justifies extra effort that saving produce does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Lower them down with a rope.
Disrupting the learning in the study hall.
It is fine, meaning it is permitted.

phrases.english: Here we learned: he may not lower them with a rope through the windows,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in round brackets. Either way, this is the rule for a roof with no skylight.

phrases.english: and he may not bring them down by way of ladders.
There, what is the law?
Here, on יום טוב, it is forbidden
because there is no disruption of the בית המדרש;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שַׁבָּת, דְּאִיכָּא בִּטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
phrases.english: but on שבת, where there is a disruption of the בית המדרש,
it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא תְּנַן: לֹא יְשַׁלְשְׁלֵם בְּחֶבֶל בְּחַלּוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a second question on the same pattern as Steps 5 and 6, now about ropes and ladders.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether sacks may be lowered through windows or down ladders on שבת for the sake of the בית המדרש.

steps.title: The other side again, and the question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the opposite reasoning: on יום טוב, where produce may be lost, ropes and ladders are still forbidden, so on שבת, with no loss, they should be even more forbidden. No answer is found, and the question ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: here, where produce may be lost, you say it is not allowed. There, where nothing is lost, isn't it all the more forbidden? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the rope-and-ladder question and then says תיקו. The question is left without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons pull in opposite directions. The מצוה of learning on שבת might allow more, but on יום טוב there is a real risk of loss, which on שבת there is not. The גמרא cannot decide which reason is stronger, so it leaves the question open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: Both questions compare שבת with יום טוב. The מצוה of learning on שבת might allow more, but the risk of losing produce on יום טוב is a reason שבת does not have. The rope-and-ladder question ends in תיקו.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. "Here" (הכא) is always the יום טוב case of produce on the roof. "There" (התם) is always the שבת case of clearing sacks for guests or learning.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: הָכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶפְסֵד פֵּירוֹת
phrases.english: Or perhaps: here, where there is a loss of produce,
you say no,
there, where there is no loss of produce,
is it not all the more so?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא: הָכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶפְסֵד פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question from Step 7 and closes it with תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the lack of loss on שבת makes lowering by rope or ladder even more forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיקו: the rope-and-ladder question for שבת is left unresolved.

steps.title: עולא: covering is allowed even for bricks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one may cover produce on יום טוב. עולא says this applies even to a row of bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and one may cover the produce. עולא said: and even a row of bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, about covering produce to protect it from a leak. עולא widens the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only produce. עולא says the permission is not limited to food. Even bricks, which could be ruined by the rain, may be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: We cover, meaning one may cover.

phrases.english: And one may cover the produce.
עולא said: and even a row of bricks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission to cover produce also includes things like bricks.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: only produce that is fit for use
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק disagrees with עולא. Only produce that is fit for use may be covered, not bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: only produce that is fit for use.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק argues with עולא and limits the משנה's permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק, the משנה said "produce" on purpose. It means things that can be used on יום טוב. Bricks are meant for building and cannot be used on יום טוב, so they may not be covered.

phrases.english: רבי יצחק said: produce that is fit for use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with עולא's wider reading in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only produce that is fit for use may be covered, not bricks.

steps.title: רבי יצחק is consistent with his own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יצחק's view matches another rule he taught: a vessel may be moved only for something that itself may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק follows his own reasoning, for רבי יצחק said: a vessel may be moved only for the sake of something that may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יצחק's view by pointing to another rule he taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering something means moving a cloth, which is a vessel. רבי יצחק holds that you may move a vessel only for the sake of something that may itself be moved. Bricks are מוקצה, so you may not move a cloth to cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning he is consistent with another view of his.
Something that may be moved on שבת, meaning it is not מוקצה.

steps.whatToRemember: עולא allows covering anything that could be ruined, even bricks. רבי יצחק allows covering only usable produce, because a vessel may be moved only for the sake of something that is not מוקצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the יום טוב covering rule to a general rule about moving vessels for the sake of מוקצה items.

phrases.english: And רבי יצחק follows his own reasoning.
For רבי יצחק said:
A vessel may not be moved
phrases.notes: The "vessel" here is the cloth used to cover things.

phrases.english: except for something that may be moved on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רבי יצחק's view from Step 10 in another rule he taught.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's limit that only usable produce may be covered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's own rule that a vessel may be moved only for the sake of something that may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה's word 'produce'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one may cover produce, and reads it as excluding bricks. That would support רבי יצחק against עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: one may cover produce with cloths. This suggests that produce may be covered, but a row of bricks may not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה's wording as a proof for רבי יצחק: the משנה specifically says 'produce.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any item could be covered, why did the משנה say 'produce'? The exact word seems to teach that only usable things like produce may be covered. Bricks may not be moved on יום טוב, so they would be left out. That fits רבי יצחק and goes against עולא.

phrases.english: We learned: One may cover produce with cloths.
phrases.notes: Here כלים means cloths or coverings, not dishes.

phrases.english: Produce, yes,
a row of bricks, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the מחלוקת of עולא and רבי יצחק by testing it against the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's view that only usable items, and not bricks, may be covered
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's specific wording 'מְכַסִּין אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת'

steps.title: 'Produce' was only said to match the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. Bricks may also be covered. The משנה said 'produce' only to match its earlier clause about lowering produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the same is true even for a row of bricks. But since the first clause taught 'one may lower produce,' the later clause also said 'one may cover produce.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The word 'produce' does not come to exclude bricks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, about lowering through a skylight, really is limited to produce, since bricks may not be handled at all. The משנה simply kept the same word in the next clause about covering. So the wording proves nothing, and עולא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he taught (so the wording just follows along)
One may lower (produce through a window)

phrases.english: The same is true even for a row of bricks,
and since he taught in the first clause 'one may lower produce,'

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי מְכַסִּין אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: he also taught in the later clause 'one may cover produce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference drawn from the word 'produce'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word was chosen to match the earlier clause, not to exclude bricks.

steps.title: A second proof from wine jugs and oil jugs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה's mention of wine jugs and oil jugs. These are usable items, which again suggests that only usable things may be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: and similarly jugs of wine and jugs of oil may be covered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for רבי יצחק, using the משנה's next examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's examples, wine and oil, are things a person can use on יום טוב. This suggests the rule of covering is limited to usable things. Bricks are not usable, so they would not be included.

phrases.english: We learned: and similarly jugs of wine
and similarly jugs of oil!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְכֵן כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכֵן כַּדֵּי שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof is rejected, a second proof is brought from the same משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's examples of wine jugs and oil jugs, which are usable items

steps.title: The jugs hold untithed wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The משנה may be talking about jugs of טבל, which may not be used. So the משנה would allow covering unusable items, just like bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Jugs holding untithed wine and oil (טבל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof by explaining that the jugs in the משנה contain טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל may not be used until it is tithed, and tithing is not allowed on יום טוב. So טבל is מוקצה, just like bricks. Read this way, the משנה actually supports עולא: even unusable items may be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Produce that has not been tithed yet and may not be used

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this answer only keeps the question open. If the jugs are טבל, the משנה would actually show that unusable things may be covered, which is עולא's view.

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
With untithed (טבל) wine and oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the jugs hold usable wine and oil
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The jugs may hold טבל, which is unusable, just like bricks.

steps.title: Why the טבל reading makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the טבל reading. If the jugs held permitted wine and oil, the משנה would be repeating what it already said about produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you thought the משנה meant jugs of permitted wine and oil, it already taught 'produce' in the first clause! Why repeat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer from step 15 with an argument that otherwise the משנה would be saying something extra for no reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitted wine and oil are usable food, just like produce. The משנה already allowed covering produce, so listing the jugs would add nothing new. That suggests the jugs must be a new case: טבל, which is unusable.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (this supports the previous answer)
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: So too it makes sense,
for if you were to think
that the jugs of wine and jugs of oil are permitted,
didn't he already teach 'produce' in the first clause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the טבל answer from step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the jugs contain טבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה would otherwise be repeating its own case of produce

steps.title: The jugs were needed to teach about a small loss
steps.stepSummary: The support is rejected. Even permitted jugs needed to be mentioned. Otherwise we might think the חכמים allowed covering only for a big loss, not for the smaller loss of drips into a jug.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wine and oil jugs needed to be mentioned. You might have thought the חכמים cared only about a big loss, like produce, and not a small loss, like drips into a jug. The משנה teaches us that the jugs may be covered too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the argument of step 16. Mentioning the jugs teaches something new even if they hold permitted wine and oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain can ruin produce, which is a big loss. A few drops falling into a wine or oil jug cause only a small loss. Without the jugs in the משנה, we might have thought covering is allowed only for big losses. So the jugs could still be permitted ones, and the משנה does not settle the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: Neither proof from the משנה works. The word 'produce' only matches the earlier clause, and the jugs can be explained either way. So the מחלוקת between עולא and רבי יצחק is not settled by this משנה.

phrases.aramaic: כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil were necessary for him to teach,
since you might have thought:
for a large loss, they were concerned;
for a small loss, they were not concerned;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that permitted jugs would make the משנה repeat itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The jugs teach that covering is allowed even for a small loss, which 'produce' alone would not have shown.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about a bucket under a leak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that allows putting a vessel under a leak on שבת. Leak water seems unusable, so this seems to contradict רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: one may put a vessel under a leak on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק with a משנה. The משנה lets you move a bucket to catch leaking water, and that water seems to be something you may not use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק holds that a כלי may be moved only for the sake of something that may itself be moved on שבת. Dirty leak water seems unusable, which makes it מוקצה. If the משנה lets you bring a bucket for it, that seems to go against his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A leak, water dripping from the roof

phrases.english: We learned: one may place a vessel
under a leak on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַדֶּלֶף בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of the משנה ends, a new series of challenges against רבי יצחק begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that a כלי is moved only for something that may itself be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leak water seems unusable, yet the משנה allows moving a vessel for it.

steps.title: The leak water is usable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about leak water that is fit to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a leak whose water is fit to use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means water that is fit to use, so it is not מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water can be used, for example for drinking, then the bucket is being moved for something usable. That fits רבי יצחק's rule perfectly.

phrases.english: With a leak that is fit.
phrases.notes: He means the dripping water is clean enough to be used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows a vessel even for unusable leak water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking only about usable water.

steps.title: Challenge from covering bricks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading a mat over bricks on שבת, even though bricks seem unusable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may spread a mat over bricks on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. A ברייתא allows moving a mat to cover bricks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building bricks are normally מוקצה. If you may move a mat to protect them, it seems a כלי can be moved for something unusable, which goes against רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for bringing a source

phrases.english: Come and hear: one may spread a mat
over bricks on שבת!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי לְבֵנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bricks are unusable, yet you may move a mat to cover them.

steps.title: Leftover bricks can be sat on
steps.stepSummary: The bricks are leftovers from building, so they are usable as seats.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are bricks left over from building, which are fit to sit on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these bricks are no longer meant for building, so people use them as seats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the building is done, extra bricks become ordinary objects for sitting. Since they are usable, the mat is moved for something usable, and רבי יצחק's rule holds.

phrases.english: That were left over from the building,
which are fit to sit on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means ordinary building bricks, which are מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means leftover bricks that are used for sitting.

steps.title: Challenge from covering stones
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading a mat over stones, which are normally מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may spread a mat over stones on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge. A ברייתא allows covering stones with a mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stones are a standard example of מוקצה. Protecting them with a mat seems to mean moving a כלי for something unusable.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one may spread a mat
over stones on שבת!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי אֲבָנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against the same rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stones are unusable, yet a mat may be moved to cover them.

steps.title: Rounded stones for the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The stones are rounded ones used for wiping in the bathroom, so they are usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about rounded stones, which are fit for use in the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these are smooth, rounded stones that people used for cleaning themselves in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stones like these have a use on שבת, so they are not מוקצה. Covering them means moving the mat for something usable.

phrases.english: With rounded stones,
which are fit for the bathroom.
phrases.notes: In those days, smooth stones were used for wiping, the way we use toilet paper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means ordinary מוקצה stones.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means rounded stones that are usable in the bathroom.

steps.title: Challenge from covering a beehive
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading a mat over a beehive against sun or rain, as long as he does not mean to trap the bees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may spread a mat over a beehive on שבת. In the sun, it is done because of the sun, and in the rain, because of the rain, as long as he does not intend to trap!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth challenge. A beehive with bees is not usable on שבת, yet a mat may be moved to protect it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hive and the bees are מוקצה, so moving a mat for them seems to break רבי יצחק's rule. The ברייתא's only limit is about trapping, which is a separate מלאכה, and it says nothing about מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: To trap, a forbidden מלאכה on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The condition 'as long as he does not intend to trap' is about the separate איסור of trapping. It is not the answer to the מוקצה question, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one may spread a mat
over a beehive on שבת,
in the sun, because of the sun,
and in the rain, because of the rain,
as long as he does not intend to trap!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי כַּוֶּרֶת דְּבוֹרִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth challenge against the same rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A beehive is unusable on שבת, yet a mat may be moved to protect it.

steps.title: The hive has honey in it
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the hive contains honey, which is usable, so the mat is moved for something usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is talking about a hive that has honey in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hive has honey inside, and honey can be eaten on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mat is really protecting the honey, which is something usable. So like the leak, the bricks and the stones, this case fits רבי יצחק's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: There too, the same answer applies there

steps.whatToRemember: All four challenges get the same kind of answer: the thing being protected is actually usable on שבת. The honey answer is challenged right away in the next step, and the discussion of the beehive continues from there.

phrases.english: There too, it is where there is honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 and completes the series of answers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mat is moved for an unusable beehive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mat protects honey, which is usable.

steps.title: What about the rainy season, when there is no honey?
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא ממישן asks רב אשי how the honey answer can work in the winter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא from מישן said to רב אשי: Your answer works in the summer, when the hive has honey. But in the rainy season, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא challenges the answer from Step 25. That answer only works when there is honey in the hive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed the mat both against the sun and against the rain. Rain means winter, when hives usually have no honey. So the honey answer seems to fail for half the case.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one case, but not for the other)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא מִמֵּישָׁן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Ukva from Meishan said to Rav Ashi:
This works well in the summer,
when there is honey.
In the rainy season, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the honey answer from Step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the hive holds usable honey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא covers the rainy season too, and there is no honey then, so the hive should be מוקצה.

steps.title: The two honeycombs left in winter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed for the two honeycombs that stay in the hive during winter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for those two honeycombs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even in winter, the hive is not empty. Two honeycombs remain in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Those two honeycombs' are the ones that stay in the hive over the winter. Because there is still some honey, the mat is again being moved for something usable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this case)

phrases.english: It is needed only
for those two honeycombs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָן שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In winter the hive has no honey, so nothing usable is inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two honeycombs stay in the hive in winter, so something usable is still there.

steps.title: Those two honeycombs are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two winter honeycombs are themselves מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But those two honeycombs are מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 27. Those honeycombs are set aside, so they do not count as usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two honeycombs are left for the bees, not for people. A person has no plan to use them. So they are מוקצה, and they cannot make the hive count as usable.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, not ready to use on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Those two honeycombs are מוקצה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two honeycombs make the hive usable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Honeycombs left for the bees are set aside from human use, so they are מוקצה themselves.

steps.title: He planned beforehand to take them
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the owner planned before שבת to take the honeycombs.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he had them in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case. The owner planned ahead of time to use those honeycombs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner decides before שבת to use them, the honeycombs are no longer set aside. So they are not מוקצה, and the hive holds something usable again.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a case)
He had them in mind, he planned to use them

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where he had them in mind.
phrases.notes: He means he decided before שבת that he would take these honeycombs to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The winter honeycombs are left for the bees, so they are מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He planned before שבת to take them, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: Why didn't the ברייתא state this condition?
steps.stepSummary: If not planning would make it forbidden, the ברייתא should have said so instead of adding a condition about trapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did not have them in mind, what? Is it forbidden? Then instead of teaching 'as long as he does not mean to trap', it should make a distinction inside this case itself: When is this said? When he had them in mind. But if he did not have them in mind, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 29. If the whole heter depends on planning ahead, the ברייתא should have said that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ends with a condition: 'as long as he does not mean to trap.' The גמרא argues that a more basic condition was needed first, namely that he planned to take the honeycombs. Since the ברייתא never mentions planning, it seems the ברייתא is not talking about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it make a distinction within the case itself
When is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא חִשֵּׁב עֲלֵיהֶם מַאי — אָסוּר?
phrases.english: But if he did not have them in mind, what? Is it forbidden?
Instead of teaching: 'As long as he does not mean to trap,'
let it make a distinction and teach within the case itself:
When is this said? When he had them in mind;
but if he did not have them in mind, it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּין לָצוּד לִפְלוֹג וְלִתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from Step 29 using the wording of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about a case where he planned to take the honeycombs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If planning were the key condition, the ברייתא should have stated it before adding an extra condition about trapping.

steps.title: Even when he planned, he must not mean to trap
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means: even if he planned to take them, it is allowed only if he does not mean to trap.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: Even if he had them in mind, it is still allowed only as long as he does not mean to trap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. The planning is assumed, and the trapping condition is added on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already takes for granted that the honeycombs are not מוקצה. Its point is a second limit: even then, the person may not intend to trap the bees. So the trapping condition does not replace the planning condition. It adds to it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (rereading a text)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Even if he had them in mind,
it is allowed only as long as he does not mean to trap.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחִשֵּׁב עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 30
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trapping condition was mentioned in place of the planning condition, so planning is not part of the case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Planning is assumed. The trapping condition is an extra limit even when he planned.

steps.title: The ברייתא now follows two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: This reading follows רבי יהודה on מוקצה in the first part and רבי שמעון on unintended acts at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the ברייתא? Following רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה? But say the end of it: 'As long as he does not mean to trap.' Now we have come to רבי שמעון, who says that an unintended act is allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole explanation. The ברייתא cannot follow one תנא in one half and the opposing תנא in the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worrying about מוקצה at all fits רבי יהודה. But allowing the act as long as he does not mean to trap fits רבי שמעון, who holds that דבר שאין מתכוון is permitted. רבי יהודה forbids an unintended act. So the reading built in Steps 25 through 31 splits the ברייתא between two opposing views.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) it?
Say the last part of the text
We have come to (the view of)
An act done without meaning to cause the forbidden result

steps.whatToRemember: The whole line of answers (honey, the two honeycombs, planning ahead) assumes רבי יהודה's view of מוקצה. The ברייתא's final words about not meaning to trap, however, match רבי שמעון. So the explanation now looks split between the two.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two arguments. רבי יהודה holds of מוקצה and forbids an unintended act. רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה and permits an unintended act. The problem is that the ברייתא seems to take one position from each of them.

phrases.english: How did you set it up?
Like Rabbi Yehuda, who holds of מוקצה?
Say the last part:
'As long as he does not mean to trap.'
We have come to Rabbi Shimon,
who says: an unintended act is allowed!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאִית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the whole explanation built in Steps 25 through 31
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה's view of מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the ברייתא permits an unintended act, which is רבי שמעון's view, so the ברייתא would follow two opposing תנאים.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון forbids an act whose result is certain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the end of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. אביי and רבא both say that רבי שמעון agrees an act is forbidden when its forbidden result is certain, and covering a beehive certainly traps the bees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think the end of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון? Didn't אביי and רבא both say that רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and it won't die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from the last step that the end of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows an unintended forbidden act only when that act might not happen. If you cover a beehive, the bees are trapped for sure, so this is a פסיק רישיה. In that kind of case even רבי שמעון forbids it, so his opinion cannot explain why the ברייתא allows covering the hive.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? A phrase that rejects a suggestion
Two major אמוראים who often appear together
'Cut off its head and it won't die?' A name for an act whose forbidden result is certain to happen

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's leniency about unintended acts does NOT cover every act done without intent. It only covers cases where the forbidden result might not happen. When the result is certain (פסיק רישיה), he forbids it too.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that even רבי שמעון forbids a פסיק רישיה is a key principle in the laws of שבת. It limits how far the leniency of 'not intending' can go.

phrases.english: And can you really think it follows Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He means the end of the ברייתא, 'provided he does not intend to trap', which step 32 linked to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye and Rava
both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
phrases.notes: If the forbidden result is sure to happen, it's forbidden even if you don't mean it. Covering the hive surely traps the bees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? וְהָא אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 32's split reading by showing that רבי שמעון cannot explain the end of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the end of the ברייתא ('provided he does not intend to trap') follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Covering a beehive certainly traps the bees, which makes it a פסיק רישיה. אביי and רבא say that even רבי שמעון forbids a פסיק רישיה, so his opinion cannot be the basis for allowing it.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה: the hive has extra openings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. The case is a hive that has small openings, so covering it does not certainly trap the bees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. The case here is a hive that has windows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the split reading and says the whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It explains that the hive in the case has small side openings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the hive has other openings, covering the top does not trap the bees for sure. So this is no longer a פסיק רישיה. Making the whole ברייתא follow one תנא also removes the problem from step 32 of mixing two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. It introduces the גמרא's true position after other ideas were rejected
What case are we dealing with here? It introduces a narrower case setting

phrases.english: Actually, all of it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and with what case are we dealing here?
Where it has windows.
phrases.notes: He means small openings in the beehive, so the bees can still get out after the top is covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 and also the split-opinion problem from step 32 by assigning the whole ברייתא to רבי יהודה and narrowing the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) and reassigning the ברייתא to a single תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was thought to mix רבי יהודה (on מוקצה) with רבי שמעון (on unintended acts). Covering the hive was assumed to trap the bees for sure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. The hive has side openings, so covering it does not certainly trap the bees.

steps.title: The wording 'provided he does not intend to trap' cannot stand for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא now follows רבי יהודה, the גמרא says not to read its ending as 'provided he does not intend to trap.' This prepares a corrected wording, which comes at the top of the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, do not read 'provided he does not intend to trap.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a fix to the ברייתא's wording. It says that the phrase about intent does not fit רבי יהודה, and the corrected reading comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that an unintended forbidden act is still forbidden, so intent cannot be what makes something allowed in his view. That means the words 'provided he does not intend' do not fit a ברייתא that follows him. The גמרא must replace them with wording that does not depend on intent.

keyTerms.meaning: And do not say. It introduces a change in how a text is read
To trap. One of the forbidden types of work on שבת

phrases.english: And do not say, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
'provided he does not intend to trap,'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא תֵּימָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּין לָצוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the answer of step 34 forward by adjusting the ברייתא's wording so that it fits רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the text's wording (setup; the corrected wording follows next)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ending of the ברייתא makes the permission depend on the person's intent.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, intent cannot be what decides it, so that wording is set aside and a corrected reading will be given.
